cause: Context Pack was frozen before development started.
impact: The line has an evidence-bound starting context.
lesson: Freeze the initial context before changing implementation state.

cause: The frozen objective item 4 asked block 1 to keep POST /runs and POST /runs/batch validation-symmetric for the new survey design fields. That assumed the batch endpoint accepts the same parameter set. It does not: batch_run_endpoint takes only project_root, mode, y_list, x, file, sheet_name and transpose, and does not even accept model_type. The v1.6.9 symmetry debt concerned parameters the two endpoints share, not batch accepting every parameter.
impact: A test written to the objective's wording would have failed because the patch seam does not exist on the batch path, not because the feature is missing, which breaks the TDD requirement that a red test fail for the right reason. Separately this exposed a real defect: FastAPI drops unknown form fields silently, so declaring strata and PSU on /runs/batch today yields a whole batch of runs computed as simple random samples with no indication anything was discarded.
lesson: Verify the seam a red test depends on before writing the assertion. A test that fails because the harness is wrong looks identical in the summary to one that fails because the feature is missing, and only the second is TDD evidence.

cause: Two regressions escaped the targeted tests and only the full suite caught them. First, _normalize_labels returned the new measurement_level key unconditionally, changing the labels payload shape for every run including those that never declared it. Second, the new arguments were passed to executor.submit by keyword, which broke existing test doubles that spy it as fake_submit(fn, *args).
impact: A block whose defining constraint is zero behaviour had in fact changed observable behaviour for all runs, and had made an existing test double invalid. The dedicated block-1 tests all passed while both defects were present.
lesson: In a zero-behaviour block, adding an always-present field is itself a behaviour change: emit new keys only when the caller declared them. And when a new argument breaks an existing test double, fix the call rather than widening the double -- appending positionally at the tail of the signature preserved both argument order and every existing spy, whereas changing the double to accept the call would have adjusted the test to fit the implementation.

cause: Block 1 wires eight complex-survey-design declarations plus measurement_level from HTTP, batch and CLI through run_service and the orchestrator into ctx.artifacts, with no consumer and no semantics.
impact: A1 and A2 both needed to extend the same run entry points, so they were not disjoint workflows. With the shared wiring landed as one zero-behaviour change, they can now proceed in parallel. Full backend suite 4638 passed / 2 skipped / 1 xfailed against a 4631 baseline (+7 new tests, no regressions); golden 17 passed with no golden file modified.
lesson: A shared thin-wiring commit is worth its own block when two lanes would otherwise contend for the same entry points, but only if it is verified to be genuinely inert -- the load-bearing evidence is a run declaring every new field being bit-identical to one declaring none, not the absence of obvious behaviour.
